title: Tensor evaluation and unit comparison on the one-point ring site
statement: For a commutative ring A, use the one-point bottom-topology ring site and its module sheaves from [def-weil-pbc-ring-complex-cech-data], with the sheaf tensor structure used by [def-weil-pbc-ringed-extended-cech]. Evaluation F at the unique object admits a natural A-linear tensor isomorphism F(M) tensor_A F(N) to F(M tensor N). Construct this comparison from the sheafification unit and the sheaf tensor presentation. For morphisms f:M to Mprime and g:N to Nprime its naturality square is F(f tensor g) after the comparison equals the comparison after f tensor g on evaluated modules. For every x in F(M), the comparison with the ring unit takes 1 tensor x to F(left-unitor inverse)(x). All comparison data and inverse identities are constructed and proved.

proof.text: Every presheaf on the bottom topology is a sheaf. Apply Adjunction.isIso_unit_app_of_iso to the sheafification adjunction and the presheaf tensor of the two underlying module sheaves. Compose its unit with the underlying inverse of tensorObjIsoSheafification. This is an isomorphism; construct the inverse explicitly using the inverse of that presheaf comparison. Evaluation gives the required ordinary module tensor isomorphism.

The whiskering naturality formulas for tensorObjIsoSheafification give its naturality square. Compose with the naturality square of the adjunction unit, then evaluate at the unique object. The presheaf tensor map evaluates to TensorProduct.map of the two evaluated linear maps.

Express the inverse tensor presentation with the monoidal structure maps of sheafification. Naturality of the left unitor and the monoidal functor left-unitor identity identify its composite with the sheaf left unitor with the sheafification of the presheaf left unitor followed by the adjunction counit. Compose with the adjunction unit; naturality and the right triangle identity cancel the adjunction. Evaluating gives the ordinary module left unitor, which sends 1 tensor x to x. Cancel the invertible evaluated sheaf left unitor to obtain the asserted inverse-unitor formula.
